A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAKTON framework and study. Their main text, tables, figures, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original ContractNLI classification and LegalBench-RAG retrieval results, retrieval ablations, a human preference study, and G-EVAL assessments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds statistical analysis comparing human and G-EVAL judgment distributions.

M1.justification: The Archivist–Researcher–Interrogator architecture, hierarchical chunking, hybrid retrieval, reranking, and iterative report refinement remain unchanged. Newly printed refinement prompts and expanded descriptions document existing operations rather than establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ContractNLI classification, retrieval over PrivacyQA, ContractNLI, MAUD, and CUAD, and the same human-study and G-EVAL scenarios. The full-contract and isolated-span evaluations already appear in v1.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same Saul and prompting baselines, Naive/RCTS retrieval with and without Cohere reranking, and GPT-4o comparison system. The detailed appendix baseline tables also retain their comparator membership.

E3.justification: New Appendix C.1 introduces a protocol for comparing evaluators: convert G-EVAL scores into categorical votes using a less-than-1% tie threshold, exclude uncertain human responses, and normalize distributions. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged; disclosure that human responses were system-labeled does not establish a newly changed study design.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1 adds evaluator-agreement analysis and a sensitivity analysis excluding Contextual and Legal Understanding. Existing reranker and LLM-filtering ablations, character-versus-span evaluation, retrieval-volume analysis, and the representative case study are retained.

E5.justification: v2 substantially expands statistical validation through Appendix C.1, adding variance-comparison F-tests, Kolmogorov–Smirnov and Mann–Whitney tests, and distributional similarity/error summaries for human versus automated judgments. v1 already contains model-variability statistics and repeated baseline runs; v2 does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: The benchmark tables retain their numerical results, including the detailed appendix evaluations. Section 4.1.1 revises ANOVA from F=3.05, p=0.12 to F=4.19, p=0.075, and regression slope from 0.44 to 0.33. Appendix C.1 adds agreement results, including cosine similarity 0.88 overall and 0.9164 after excluding one criterion.

T1.justification: New Appendix E introduces a formal computational-cost model absent from v1. Equations (1)–(5) derive agent-level and total LLM-call counts and decompose runtime into inference, document processing, and retrieval operations; vector-search complexity is also stated. These are analytical additions, not measured runtime results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: an open-source, modular, model-agnostic three-agent framework with specialized retrieval and explainable legal reports. Describing retrieval as multi-stage and emphasizing agent specialization clarify existing claims without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for omitting agent-removal ablations, interprets system-labeled human evaluation as reflecting real-world use, and argues that evaluator-agreement statistics reinforce validity. Appendix E adds reasoning about computational tradeoffs. The existing language, jurisdiction, latency, and structural-parsing limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly supplies system and user prompts for report refinement and points readers to the complete prompt collection. Appendix B explicitly discloses that evaluators knew each response's source. Existing hardware, retrieval hyperparameters, interrogation limits, and dataset-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for already-used model families and datasets, including Mistral, Qwen, Gemma, Llama, DeepSeek, PrivacyQA, MAUD, and CUAD. It also positions the human study against Jiang et al. (2024) and STORM and more explicitly identifies hierarchical encoding as a contribution; the main related-work discussion remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The appendices are substantially reorganized: human evaluation, G-EVAL, and the case study move ahead of retrieval and classification experiments, with a new computational-cost section between them. Appendix numbering is repaired, including the duplicated A heading, and main-text explanations and terminology receive localized editing.

P2.justification: v2 adds the regression scatterplot in Figure 3, changes Table 1 highlighting and its caption, adds boxed refinement prompts, and improves rendering of existing plots. Retained appendix figures and tables are regrouped near their discussions; their underlying benchmark displays largely remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility and auditability through refinement prompts, disclosure of the labeled human evaluation, clearer appendix organization, and corrected model-variability statistics consistent with Table 1. The cost derivation also clarifies computational dependencies. Benefits are limited by the new agreement analysis's overstrong validation claim: human and G-EVAL evaluations use different question sets, and nonsignificant distribution tests do not establish equivalence. Overall, these are useful but bounded improvements to an otherwise stable study.
